title: Stateful connection shedder and spiral fallback runbook
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Problem: During regional surges and downstream pressure (Redis/Kafka/postgres), our connection pools saturate and cause high tail latency and partial outages. Current mitigation (global shedding + tenant soft-quotas) is blunt: it either hurts all tenants equally or fails to preserve SLOs for high-priority workloads.

Goal: Build a stateful connection shedder that makes eviction decisions using per-connection telemetry (idle_score, recent_error_rate, downstream_replica_lag, txn_cost), coordinates with the KV-cache layer to avoid painful cache-miss amplifications, and executes a spiral fallback plan that ramps degradation in controlled phases. The runbook should include design, tests, rollout, and rollback criteria.

Scope: Implementation sits in the connection pool manager (co-located with runtime worker), influences admission and eviction order, exposes metrics/events for Console, and integrates with regional failover routing for multi-region continuity.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New shedder reduces 95th/99th token latency tail by >= 20% under simulated downstream overload for the critical tenant profile (bench as defined in runbook).
2) Per-tenant graceful degradation allows critical tenants to maintain SLOs while non-critical tenants degrade, validated in multi-tenant load tests.
3) Console surfaces per-pool 'eviction_pressure' and 'spiral_phase' metrics and a runbook link; alerts fire when spiral reaches phase 3.

4) Chaos test: when a Redis region is delayed by 300ms/50% error rate, spiral fallback automatically engages and traffic shifts to fallback region for read-path within configured TTL without cache stampede.
5) Feature flagged rollout with canary (10% hosts) and automatic rollback criteria (error surge > 5x baseline OR >10% of requests returned degraded when not expected).
design_decisions: Eviction scoring: combine idle_score (40%), recent_error_rate (30%), txn_cost_estimate (20%), and tenant_priority (10%) to produce a single eviction_rank. This keeps scoring explainable and tunable.
Stateful vs stateless: choose stateful per-host shedder so eviction decisions can be computed with local connection history, avoiding cross-host coordination which increases latency and complexity.

Spiral fallback phases: Phase 0 (monitoring), Phase 1 (soft-shed lowest eviction_rank), Phase 2 (aggressive shedding + hedged reads), Phase 3 (regional failover & cache bypass with degraded responses). Phases escalate based on 'eviction_pressure' percentile and sustained downstream error rate.

KV-cache integration: communicate 'latency_sensitive' flag to KV cache. If a connection is a candidate for eviction and request is cacheable with recent prefix hit, prefer skipping eviction for that connection to avoid cache stampede.
Admission control: augment token-bucket with a fast path for high-priority tenants and a slow path otherwise. Admission uses per-tenant budget and global pressure adjustments.
Fallback model variants: prefer model-quantized or shorter-context variants for degraded mode to preserve latency budgets rather than throttling requests entirely.
Telemetry: expose eviction_reason labels (idle, errors, cost, tenant_quota) and emit sample traces when spiral phase changes to aid post-mortem.
Tradeoffs: stateful host-local decisions can lead to uneven tenant experience across hosts; mitigate with randomized sticky routing and short rebalancing windows.
Security: no sensitive payloads are logged; only connection metadata and anonymized tenant IDs are emitted.
implementation_notes: Core changes in runtime pool manager: add eviction_score calculation, periodic pressure aggregator, and spiral state machine (code in runtime/pool/ejector.go).
Metrics to add: pool_eviction_pressure (gauge), pool_eviction_count{reason}, tenant_evicted_requests_total, spiral_phase{pool}.
PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1892 (WIP) - contains scoring algorithm and unit tests.

DB/Config: introduces a new per-tenant config flag `degradation_tier` (enum low/med/high) stored in tenant-config service; migration script PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tenant-config/pull/74.
Integration: KV-cache team to add 'protect_connection' hook (contract in runbook).
Estimated dev tasks: scoring + unit tests (2), pressure aggregator + metrics (2), spiral state machine + e2e (3), console dashboard wiring (1).
Owners: Priya Kapoor (implementation), Nora Al-Sayed (QA & load harness), Mateo Ruiz (console & alerts).
test_plan: Unit tests for eviction_score boundaries and deterministic tie-breakers.
Synthetic load: 3 region redistribution test where Redis-A latency is increased to 300ms; validate spiral engages and traffic migrates with <= 2x cache-miss spike.
Multi-tenant fairness bench: 50 tenants, ensure top-10% priority tenants keep <10% latency deviation.
Chaos suite: introduce pod restarts while spiral is active to ensure no deadlocks and no double-eviction snafus.
Load test harness results stored in: gs://redwood-benchmarks/eviction-shedder/2025-02-24/
Regression: run against canary model variants and ensure degraded variant outputs meet quality thresholds (evals suite).
rollout_plan: Alpha: enable feature flag on dev and internal canaries (2 hosts) - smoke tests.
Canary: 10% hosts, observe metrics for 48 hours. If error rate or degraded responses exceed thresholds, auto-disable flag.
Ramp: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% over 2 weeks with monitoring checkpoints.
Manual checkpoints: full regression run, SRE signoff, PM approval before >60%.
Rollback criteria: sustained increase >= 2x in user-facing errors OR tenant-SLO violations exceeding defined windows; revert flag and postmortem within 72 hours.
